channel.title: Dramora
channel.description: Every story hides a secret. Every secret changes everything.

item.title: A Little Girl Exposed the Heiress's Fake Pregnancy
item.description: Three hundred guests were applauding the announcement of the Whitmore heir when an eight-year-old said the pregnant woman had a sofa pillow under her dress. Her mother ran hotel security. She had eleven years of camera footage to prove the child was right.

item.title: A Street Child Held Out My Sister's Hair Clip. My Sister Died Nine Years Ago.
item.description: A dirty little girl reached for the jeweled clip in Evelyn Hart's hair, then opened her own hand and showed a second one — scratched, bent, and identical. Only two were ever made. The other belonged to Evelyn's sister, whose car was pulled from a ravine nine years ago with her blood inside and no body.

item.title: The Waitress Who Stopped the Billionaire's Last Drink
item.description: Nora Vale was serving table nine when she saw the bride-to-be pour something into the groom's wine. She had four minutes to decide whether keeping her job mattered more than a stranger's life.

item.title: He Ordered a DNA Test Behind My Back. The Lab Called Me First.
item.description: A lab calls Maren about DNA results she never ordered. Her husband secretly tested their nineteen-year-old daughter—and included his mother in a three-generation family panel that was supposed to settle one question but exposes a much older one.

item.title: My Husband's Assistant Wore My Perfume. I Said Nothing for Six Months.
item.description: At a company dinner, Elise recognizes her custom perfume on her husband's assistant—a scent made in only two bottles a year. She says nothing, goes home, and discovers the second bottle is missing on the same day a suspicious company transfer was approved.

item.title: She Pushed His Daughter Into the Pool. Then He Came Home Early.
item.description: Vivian threw her stepdaughter's necklace into the pool, then pushed her in after it — and told the staff no one was allowed to help. She had three hours before Adrian's flight landed. His flight landed early.

item.title: They Made the Waitress Kneel. She Owned the Building.
item.description: A VIP customer orders waitress Nora Vance onto her knees, and her regional director tells her to obey. Nora does it without protest because nobody in the restaurant knows the building belongs to her.
